why_it_matters: Firm employment growth supports the Fed’s inflation-fighting stance and reduces urgency for cuts, keeping tightening risk on the table.

title: US weekly jobless claims plunge to lowest since 1969
evidence_text: Initial jobless claims fell to 187,000 for the week ended July 18, the lowest level since September 1969.
why_it_matters: Very low claims indicate little labor-market cooling, which reduces urgency for Fed cuts and keeps attention on inflation.

title: US labor market stable; worker productivity accelerates in second ...
evidence_text: Initial jobless claims rose 1,000 to 199,000 for the week ended August 1, while continuing claims increased to 1.801 million.
why_it_matters: Claims remain low enough to suggest a still-resilient labor market, limiting the case for faster Fed easing.

title: US labor market losing momentum; May producer inflation comes in tame
evidence_text: Initial jobless claims held at 248,000, an eight-month peak that Reuters described as evidence of a softening labor market.
why_it_matters: Higher claims point to cooling labor demand, which typically supports a more dovish Fed reaction.

title: More Americans apply for unemployment benefits as layoffs settle at higher levels in recent weeks
evidence_text: Jobless claims rose by 20,000 to 243,000 for the week ending July 13, and the report noted claims were settling at a slightly higher level.
why_it_matters: A gradual rise in claims is consistent with labor-market cooling, which can make Fed cuts more likely.

title: US jobs market softening; slumping productivity boosts labor costs
evidence_text: Reuters reported that rising claims reflected a labor market gradually softening as higher interest rates cooled demand.
why_it_matters: This framing ties claims to slower demand and therefore to less pressure for the Fed to tighten.

title: FOMC statement
evidence_text: The FOMC kept the federal funds target range unchanged at its August 6 meeting.
why_it_matters: A hold signal means the Fed is not yet responding to labor cooling with immediate cuts, keeping policy data-dependent.

title: Soft July jobs report fuels skepticism over possible Fed rate hike
evidence_text: The July jobs report showed payrolls fell by 23,000, June was revised to a 20,000 gain, and the unemployment rate declined to 4.1%.
why_it_matters: Weaker payroll growth and a lower jobless rate reduce the case for near-term Fed tightening and make additional cuts easier to justify.

title: Economic Outlook and the Labor Market
evidence_text: Jefferson said the earlier policy-rate cuts had brought the target range broadly into neutral territory and he supported holding rates steady last month.
why_it_matters: A neutral-policy framing suggests the Fed is waiting for more labor and inflation data before deciding whether to ease further or hold.

title: The Fed - Inflation (PCE)
evidence_text: The Federal Reserve states that it aims for 2% inflation over the longer run as measured by the PCE price index.
why_it_matters: Any CPI/PCE reading above 2% keeps inflation above the Fed’s stated objective and generally argues for fewer cuts until price stability is more convincing.

title: Monetary Policy Report, June 2025
evidence_text: The report says 12-month PCE inflation was 2.1% in April, while core PCE was 2.5% and still somewhat elevated.
why_it_matters: A core PCE rate above target suggests the Fed may stay restrictive longer even if headline inflation improves.

title: May US PCE inflation tops 4%, leaves Fed hike on the table
evidence_text: Reuters reported that May PCE inflation rose 4.1% year over year and core PCE rose 3.4% year over year, both above the Fed’s 2% goal.
why_it_matters: Stronger-than-target PCE inflation reduces the case for easing and raises the risk that the Fed stays on hold or leans tighter.

title: Fed’s favored inflation gauge shows prices edged down in June but remain high
evidence_text: Yahoo Finance reported that June PCE fell 0.1% month over month, while year-over-year PCE remained 3.7% and core PCE 3.3%.
why_it_matters: The monthly cooling is somewhat easier for the Fed, but the still-elevated core rate keeps inflation pressure from fully supporting cuts.

title: PCE Inflation Dispersion
evidence_text: The San Francisco Fed provides updated PCE inflation dispersion data through June 2026, showing broad price changes across categories.
why_it_matters: Dispersion can make it harder for the Fed to declare inflation pressure is uniformly resolved, even when the headline rate slows.

title: Monetary Policy Report
evidence_text: The Fed reported that core nonhousing services inflation was 3.9% over the 12 months ending in May, above the range seen since mid-2025, while housing services inflation was 3.2%.
why_it_matters: Sticky core services and shelter inflation reduce the Fed’s confidence that inflation is moving sustainably to 2% and support keeping policy restrictive.

title: Speech by Governor Miran on the inflation outlook
evidence_text: Governor Miran said core nonhousing services inflation had moved sideways this year and that market-based core ex shelter inflation was running below 2.3%.
why_it_matters: A softer ex-shelter services signal would argue that underlying inflation pressure is closer to target and could justify easier policy.

title: Survey of Consumer Expectations
publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
evidence_text: The New York Fed’s survey tracks household expectations for inflation, wages, and labor market conditions through its regular release of consumer expectations data.
why_it_matters: Inflation expectations matter because the Fed watches whether expected inflation remains anchored enough to support a return to target without further tightening.

title: Consumer prices rose 2.4% annually in February, as expected
evidence_text: The February CPI report showed core CPI at 2.5% year over year, matching expectations and remaining moderate relative to prior readings.
why_it_matters: A softer core inflation print gives the Fed more room to consider easing if the broader data stay aligned with disinflation.

title: US inflation progress stalls on sticky services
evidence_text: ING argued that sticky services inflation and firm wages could keep the Fed wary of signaling aggressive cuts.
why_it_matters: If services inflation stays sticky and wages remain firm, the Fed is more likely to keep policy restrictive for longer.

title: US inflation surprise offers Warsh only brief relief
evidence_text: Reuters reported that June CPI came in much softer than expected, but that the move mainly reduced tightening pressure only temporarily.
why_it_matters: A softer inflation print supports easing, but the limited duration of the relief suggests the Fed may still keep policy restrictive if subsequent data re-accelerates.

title: Fed faced with hard choice on weak jobs, high inflation
evidence_text: Reuters said traders raised cut bets after weak jobs data, but the Fed was still expected to hold rates steady because inflation remained high.
why_it_matters: When inflation is still elevated, the Fed’s reaction function puts more weight on price stability, limiting the urgency of cuts.

title: Trading Day: Hello inflation, goodbye 2026 Fed cut
evidence_text: Markets interpreted hotter inflation and the Fed’s unchanged stance as evidence that rates are unlikely to be cut again this year.
why_it_matters: If traders push out expected cuts, financial conditions tighten and the Fed can afford to remain patient or even more restrictive.

title: US CPI and PPI Beat Estimates; Fed Rate Cut Delay Pressures
evidence_text: The report said both CPI and PPI came in above expectations and pushed traders to repriced the timing and size of future cuts.
why_it_matters: An upside inflation surprise reduces the Fed’s room to ease because it signals persistent price pressure against the inflation mandate.

title: Hot CPI Print Shakes Fed Cut Bets as Inflation Tops ...
evidence_text: The article says a hotter-than-expected CPI print sharply reduced expectations for near-term Fed cuts.
why_it_matters: If market pricing shifts toward fewer cuts, that implies the data has moved the reaction function away from easing and toward holding rates higher for longer.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
evidence_text: The FOMC held the policy rate unchanged and said it will keep assessing incoming data, the outlook, and risk balance before making further adjustments.
why_it_matters: A hold with data-dependence signals the Committee is not yet committed to easing or tightening and is waiting for clearer inflation and labor-market evidence.

title: Speech by Governor Bowman on the economy and monetary policy
evidence_text: Bowman said she still sees policy as moderately restrictive and continues to expect three rate cuts in 2026, while labor-market risks could worsen.
why_it_matters: A Fed governor explicitly favoring cuts reinforces the easing side of the reaction function when inflation is near target and employment risks rise.

title: Speech by Governor Cook on the economic outlook
evidence_text: Cook said the inflation pressures from tariffs and Middle East conflict should be short-lived and reiterated her commitment to returning inflation to 2 percent.
why_it_matters: If policymakers view the inflation bump as temporary, they are less likely to respond with tighter policy and more able to tolerate cuts.

title: Remarks on inflation, employment and monetary policy
evidence_text: Logan argued that modestly higher interest rates would better balance the risks because inflation remains too high and the labor market is solid.
why_it_matters: A policymaker favoring higher rates raises the threshold for cuts and signals concern that inflation risks dominate the dual mandate.

title: Speech by Governor Waller on the economic outlook
evidence_text: Waller said employment is near maximum sustainable level and warned that another hot core inflation reading this week would require the FOMC to consider tightening in the near term.
why_it_matters: This ties policy more closely to upside inflation surprises, which would push the reaction function toward fewer cuts or possible hikes.

title: The Federal Reserve, Economic Outlook and Monetary Policy
evidence_text: The Kansas City Fed posted a speech page for an outlook-and-policy address tied to the July 2026 period, but the provided excerpt does not include substantive policy guidance.
why_it_matters: Without clear policy content, this source adds little to the Fed reaction-function assessment beyond confirming ongoing Fed communication.

title: FOMC Minutes, June 16-17, 2026
evidence_text: The minutes said inflation was still above the 2 percent goal and highlighted tariff pass-through, higher energy costs, and AI-related demand as contributors.
why_it_matters: When inflation drivers are still active, the Fed's reaction function tilts toward keeping policy restrictive for longer.

title: The Fed - July 28-29, 2026 FOMC Meeting
evidence_text: The Federal Reserve posted the July 28-29 FOMC meeting press conference materials on its site, indicating the meeting event and communications release.
why_it_matters: The post-meeting press conference is where the Fed usually clarifies whether inflation or labor market risks are driving the policy stance.

title: FOMC Statement: March 2026
evidence_text: JPMorgan's recap said the FOMC held rates steady, kept inflation described as somewhat elevated, and left the labor market assessment only slightly changed.
why_it_matters: This framing suggests the Fed was still balancing both mandates rather than moving decisively toward cuts.

title: Fed meeting recap: July 2026
evidence_text: CNBC reported that the Fed left rates unchanged and that some FOMC members dissented in favor of a hike.
why_it_matters: Reported internal pressure for hikes implies the committee may be leaning more hawkish than a simple hold suggests.

title: Transcript of Chairman Warsh's Press Conference -- July 29, 2026
evidence_text: Warsh emphasized that the Fed has a single 2% inflation goal and repeated that the Committee will deliver price stability.
why_it_matters: Stronger emphasis on the inflation objective suggests the Fed is prioritizing price stability over near-term labor-market easing.

title: FOMC Minutes, June 16-17, 2026 - Federal Reserve
evidence_text: The Fed's minutes archive page confirms the June minutes were released on July 8, 2026.
why_it_matters: This is a release notice rather than policy content, so it has little direct effect on the reaction function.

title: Fed Rate Monitor
evidence_text: The market-implied next meeting outcome shown is a 25 bp hike, with the tool also displaying two hikes by year-end.
why_it_matters: If futures and related pricing lean toward hikes, the market is assigning higher odds to a restrictive Fed path rather than cuts.

title: Treasury yields jump as traders take out expectations for any 2026 Fed rate cuts
evidence_text: The piece says the 2-year Treasury yield rose to 3.9% as traders reduced expectations for any Fed rate cuts in 2026 and began considering hikes.
why_it_matters: Rising short-end yields and fading cut odds signal markets expect the Fed to stay tighter for longer or potentially move toward hikes.

title: 30 Day Federal Funds Futures Quotes
evidence_text: CME states that 30-day fed funds futures are used to gauge the probability of an upcoming Fed rate hike.
why_it_matters: This is the primary market instrument behind FedWatch-style pricing, so it is the cleanest direct read on whether the market is pricing cuts out or hikes in.

title: CME FedWatch Tool
evidence_text: CME’s FedWatch Tool provides market-implied probabilities for FOMC rate outcomes from fed funds futures prices.
why_it_matters: FedWatch is the standard reference for whether traders are pricing cuts, holds, or hikes into the next FOMC meetings.

title: Market Probability Tracker
evidence_text: The Atlanta Fed offers a market probability tracker that estimates policy-rate odds from market prices.
why_it_matters: A Fed-owned market-pricing tracker is useful for cross-checking whether futures are assigning more weight to cuts or hikes.

title: Federal Reserve: Extended pause guidance
evidence_text: UOB said OIS swaps were pricing about a one-third chance of a 25 bp hike at the July 29 FOMC meeting while the Fed was expected to hold rates unchanged.
why_it_matters: A higher priced hike probability implies markets were leaning toward a tighter Fed reaction function than a near-term cut.

title: FX Daily Snapshot
evidence_text: MUFG said the OIS curve priced close to a 30% chance of a hike at the July 29 meeting and judged that pricing too high given weaker labor market data.
why_it_matters: If traders price a hike despite softer labor data, the market is signaling less confidence in near-term easing.

title: Federal Open Market Committee meeting calendars and information
evidence_text: The Federal Reserve publishes the official FOMC meeting calendar and related meeting information on its website.
why_it_matters: The meeting calendar anchors which policy meeting the market is pricing and helps align OIS expectations with the Fed’s actual decision dates.

title: Monetary Policy: FOMC Minutes
evidence_text: The March 2026 minutes show the Committee left the federal funds target range at 3.50% to 3.75%.
why_it_matters: A steady target range indicates the Fed was not yet signaling imminent easing, which keeps a hike or hold skew more relevant than near-term cuts.

title: H.15 - Selected Interest Rates (Daily) - August 10, 2026
evidence_text: The Federal Reserve’s H.15 release shows the 2-year Treasury yield at 4.25% on August 10, 2026.
why_it_matters: The 2-year yield is a front-end rate that reflects how markets expect the policy path to evolve over the next several meetings.

title: Market Yield on U.S. Treasury Securities at 2-Year Constant Maturity
publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
evidence_text: FRED shows the 2-year Treasury constant-maturity yield at 4.25% on August 10, 2026.
why_it_matters: A higher 2-year yield generally implies markets are pricing a less-easy Fed path than before.

title: Treasury Yield Premiums - San Francisco Fed
publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco
evidence_text: The San Francisco Fed’s model puts the 2-year observed Treasury yield at 4.17% and the average expected overnight rate at 3.94% on August 10, 2026.
why_it_matters: The gap between the observed yield and the expected overnight rate indicates how much of the 2-year yield is tied to expected policy versus term premium.

title: Rate Expectations (2Y − Fed Funds): Chart, Current Level ...
evidence_text: The site says the 2-year Treasury yield minus the effective federal funds rate was 0.55 percentage points on August 5, 2026, down from 0.57 percentage points previously.
why_it_matters: A narrowing spread versus fed funds can signal that market pricing is moving closer to easier policy relative to the current rate.

title: Treasury yields: Traders reassess Fed rate hike bets
evidence_text: CNBC reported that the 2-year Treasury yield rose as traders reassessed odds of Fed rate hikes.
why_it_matters: When the 2-year yield rises on hike bets, it suggests the market expects a less accommodative Fed reaction function.

title: War-driven inflation fears fail to shake U.S. Treasury yield outlook
evidence_text: Reuters said bond strategists still expected the two-year Treasury yield to fall over coming months as markets abandoned bets on Fed rate hikes.
why_it_matters: Expected declines in the 2-year yield indicate pricing for a less restrictive Fed path and more scope for easing.

title: Employment Situation Summary - 2026 M07 Results
evidence_text: The BLS said nonfarm payrolls fell by 23,000 in July, the unemployment rate was 4.1%, and average hourly earnings rose 3.2% from a year earlier.
why_it_matters: Weaker payroll growth and softer wage gains reduce pressure on the Fed to keep policy restrictive or to hike further.

title: Shock Drop in US Payrolls Eases Pressure on Fed to Hike
evidence_text: Bloomberg reported that July payrolls fell unexpectedly, prior months were revised lower, and wage growth slowed to its weakest pace in nearly five years.
why_it_matters: The combination of weaker hiring, revisions, and slower wages supports a more dovish Fed reaction function.

title: VIEW Soft July jobs report fuels skepticism over possible Fed rate hike
evidence_text: Reuters said July payrolls fell by 23,000, June was revised to a smaller gain, and the unemployment rate slipped to 4.1% as participation declined.
why_it_matters: Markets and policymakers tend to read weaker payrolls and downward revisions as reducing the odds of near-term Fed tightening.

title: U.S. Employment (July 2026)
evidence_text: TD Economics said July payrolls declined by 23,000, unemployment fell to 4.1%, and year-over-year wage growth slowed to 3.2%.
why_it_matters: A soft labor report with slowing wages argues for holding or cutting rather than tightening if inflation is not reaccelerating.

title: US job growth slows sharply in June; labor force participation rate at more than 5-year low
evidence_text: Reuters reported that June payrolls rose by 57,000, well below expectations, while the unemployment rate fell to 4.2% largely because labor-force participation dropped.
why_it_matters: A clear slowdown in hiring, even with a lower unemployment rate, lowers the urgency for Fed tightening.

title: Instant View: US jobs report for March is stronger than expected, likely keeping Fed sidelines
evidence_text: Reuters said March payrolls rose by 178,000 and the unemployment rate fell to 4.3%, reinforcing expectations that the Fed would stay on hold.
why_it_matters: Stronger labor demand makes the Fed less likely to ease and more likely to maintain restrictive rates until inflation cools further.

title: US weekly jobless claims fall sharply, latest week
evidence_text: Initial jobless claims fell to 187,000 for the week ended July 18, the lowest since 1969, and came in well below economists' expectations.
why_it_matters: Lower claims signal a still-firm labor market, which reduces pressure on the Fed to cut rates quickly.

title: US labor market stable; worker productivity accelerates in second ...
evidence_text: Initial jobless claims rose slightly to 199,000 for the week ended August 1, while continuing claims increased to 1.801 million.
why_it_matters: The small rise is consistent with a labor market cooling only modestly, which keeps the Fed from needing to tighten and does not strongly force cuts.

title: Initial Claims (ICSA)
evidence_text: FRED reports initial claims at 199,000 for the week of 2026-08-01.
why_it_matters: This official time series confirms claims remain low by historical standards, which argues against an urgent easing response from the Fed.

title: More Americans apply for unemployment benefits as layoffs settle at higher levels in recent weeks
evidence_text: Jobless claims rose to 243,000 for the week ending July 13, and continuing claims increased to about 1.87 million.
why_it_matters: A higher claims trend points to a softer labor market, which increases the odds the Fed will favor cuts over hikes.

title: Jobless Claims Show Cool Labor Market Needs Fed Help
evidence_text: The report frames rising claims and higher continuing claims as evidence that the labor market is cooling and that rate cuts may be needed.
why_it_matters: If labor demand is softening, the Fed has more reason to ease policy rather than keep rates restrictive.

title: US jobs market softening; slumping productivity boosts labor costs
evidence_text: Reuters reported that initial claims rose to 242,000 as higher interest rates continued to cool demand.
why_it_matters: A cooling labor market lowers the risk of overheating, which supports a more dovish Fed stance.

title: Weak July jobs report helps case for Fed to hold rates but doesn't take hikes off the table
evidence_text: Reuters framed the July jobs report as strengthening the case to hold rates steady while leaving some risk of future hikes if labor data stabilizes.
why_it_matters: A hold-centered interpretation keeps policy in a neutral posture unless labor weakness deepens enough to justify cuts.

title: Resilient US economy posts third straight month of strong job growth in May
evidence_text: Reuters said three straight months of strong job gains showed the labor market was regaining traction.
why_it_matters: A firmer labor market reduces urgency for cuts and gives the Fed more room to keep policy restrictive if inflation remains sticky.

title: Weak jobs, declining labor force, could renew Fed debate over state of labor market
evidence_text: Reuters reported that June payroll growth of 57,000 and downward revisions to prior months could reopen debate at the Fed about labor-market weakness.
why_it_matters: Signs of softer hiring and lower labor supply can push the Fed toward an easier stance if they appear to threaten employment more than inflation.

title: Economic Outlook and the Labor Market
evidence_text: Jefferson said the policy rate had been lowered enough to be broadly in the range of neutral.
why_it_matters: If officials view policy as near neutral, they may need weaker labor data to justify further easing and stronger data to justify restraint.

title: August 2026 CPI release
evidence_text: The latest CPI release showed consumer price inflation remains above the Fed’s 2% objective, limiting room for near-term easing.
why_it_matters: A CPI reading above target reduces the Fed’s confidence that inflation is moving sustainably to 2%, which argues for fewer cuts.

title: June 2026 PCE Price Index
evidence_text: The June PCE report showed headline inflation easing to 3.7% year over year and core PCE easing to 3.3% year over year.
why_it_matters: Easing PCE inflation supports eventual cuts, but the level remains well above target and does not by itself justify a hawkish pivot.

title: July FOMC statement
publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
evidence_text: The FOMC kept the policy rate unchanged and said it needs more confidence that inflation is moving sustainably toward 2%.
why_it_matters: When the Fed explicitly ties cuts to further inflation progress, it signals a restrictive bias until data improve.

title: July 2026 PCE inflation press coverage of the BEA release
evidence_text: Market coverage emphasized that inflation remained too hot for the Fed to relax policy aggressively.
why_it_matters: If market participants read the PCE report as sticky inflation, that raises the hurdle for additional easing.

title: July 2026 Fed reaction-function speech on inflation
evidence_text: Logan said current inflation was still well above target and that modestly higher rates would better balance the Fed’s risks.
why_it_matters: That reaction-function framing is clearly hawkish and implies the bar for cuts remains high.

title: Monetary Policy Report, July 2026
evidence_text: The Fed said core price inflation was 3.4% in May, housing services inflation was 3.2%, and core nonhousing services inflation was 3.9% over the prior 12 months.
why_it_matters: Sticky core services and shelter inflation are central to the Fed’s reaction function because they signal incomplete progress back to 2%.

title: Survey of Consumer Expectations
publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
evidence_text: The New York Fed’s consumer expectations survey provides current measures of inflation expectations across near-, medium-, and longer-term horizons.
why_it_matters: Inflation expectations matter because the Fed watches whether they remain anchored near 2% or begin to drift higher.

title: Inflation Nowcasting
evidence_text: The Cleveland Fed’s nowcasting tool provides short-term estimates for CPI and PCE inflation before the official releases.
why_it_matters: Near-term inflation tracking helps gauge whether sticky services and shelter are likely to keep the Fed cautious.

title: The Recent U.S. Inflation Experience
publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
evidence_text: The St. Louis Fed provides background analysis on the inflation episode and its components, including services and housing dynamics.
why_it_matters: This kind of background framing is useful for interpreting whether current services inflation is likely to be persistent enough to affect policy.

title: A Faster Convergence of Shelter Prices and Market Rent: Implications for Inflation
evidence_text: The Boston Fed argued that shelter inflation could converge more quickly toward market rent measures, which would lower measured inflation over time.
why_it_matters: If shelter disinflation continues, it would support a more dovish Fed stance by improving the trajectory of core inflation.

title: US inflation surprise offers Warsh only brief relief
evidence_text: Reuters reported that June inflation cooled more than expected, but market interest-rate futures still responded by scaling back Fed tightening expectations less than before.
why_it_matters: A softer inflation print can support cuts, but the market reaction matters more here because the Fed reaction function is driven by whether disinflation is convincing enough to keep easing on track.

title: Elevated inflation will likely delay interest rate cuts this year, warns Federal Reserve Chair Powell
evidence_text: Powell said persistent inflation is likely to postpone rate cuts and that the Fed can keep rates elevated as long as needed if inflation does not ease further.
why_it_matters: This directly raises the bar for cuts because it signals the Fed prioritizes sustained inflation progress before easing policy.

title: Hot CPI Print Shakes Fed Cut Bets as Inflation Tops ...
evidence_text: A hotter-than-expected July CPI release pushed market pricing away from near-term Fed cuts.
why_it_matters: An upside inflation surprise reduces confidence that inflation is on a clean path to 2%, which argues for fewer or later cuts.

title: Fed rate cut unlikely; would be 'like throwing oil on the fire' of ...
evidence_text: Commentary cited outside experts arguing that the Fed is unlikely to cut rates at the upcoming meeting and that a hike case is stronger than a cut case.
why_it_matters: If market and analyst expectations shift toward no cuts or hikes, the Fed gets less room to ease without surprising financial conditions.

title: Fed officials' concerns about inflation sparked talk of rate hike
evidence_text: NBC reported that inflation concerns among Fed officials have revived discussion of a possible rate hike, even though no change was expected at the next meeting.
why_it_matters: Renewed hike discussion signals a more restrictive reaction function, making additional cuts less likely unless inflation data improve.

title: Speech by Governor Waller on the economic outlook
evidence_text: Waller said another hot core inflation reading would require the FOMC to consider tightening policy in the near term.
why_it_matters: This signals a reaction function that is becoming more sensitive to inflation upside surprises, which reduces the odds of additional cuts.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
evidence_text: The FOMC said it kept the target range unchanged, noted inflation remained somewhat elevated, and said it would assess incoming data before making further adjustments.
why_it_matters: This is a classic wait-and-see stance that neither clearly supports imminent cuts nor tightening.

title: Outlook for the Economy and Monetary Policy
evidence_text: Bowman said she still saw policy as moderately restrictive and expected three rate cuts in 2026, while inflation should fade as tariff effects wane.
why_it_matters: A forecast of multiple cuts and confidence in disinflation supports a more easing-leaning reaction function.

title: Economic Outlook and Supply-Side (Dis)Inflation Dynamics
evidence_text: Jefferson said prior rate cuts were responses to downside employment risks and that the policy stance should help stabilize the labor market while inflation moves toward 2 percent.
why_it_matters: This frames cuts as appropriate when labor-market risks dominate, which is consistent with an easing bias.

title: Transcript of Chairman Warsh's Press Conference -- July 29, 2026
evidence_text: The July FOMC left the policy rate unchanged at 3.50% to 3.75% in a 9-3 vote, while stating that job gains have kept pace with the workforce and inflation remains elevated relative to the 2% goal.
why_it_matters: A hold with elevated inflation language and three hike dissents points to a less-dovish reaction function and reduces the odds of near-term cuts.

title: FOMC Minutes, June 16-17, 2026
evidence_text: The June minutes said inflation remained elevated relative to the Committee's 2% goal and showed all members agreed to keep the policy rate at 3.50% to 3.75%.
why_it_matters: When inflation is still described as elevated and the Committee holds steady unanimously, the reaction function stays biased toward patience or additional restraint rather than cuts.

title: FOMC Press Conference, April 29, 2026
evidence_text: At the April press conference, the Chair said unemployment had been little changed and inflation had moved up and remained elevated, while the Committee kept rates unchanged.
why_it_matters: A still-firm labor market and higher inflation argue against immediate easing and support a wait-and-see stance.

title: Fed meeting recap: July 2026
evidence_text: CNBC reported that the Fed again held rates steady and that some participants wanted to hike, framing inflation as the dominant policy concern over the labor market.
why_it_matters: This reinforces the reading that the Committee is leaning against cuts because inflation risks are still overshadowing employment concerns.

title: U.S. FOMC Meeting Minutes (June 17, 2026)
evidence_text: TD said the minutes showed officials remained concerned that inflation was still above target while labor-market conditions were roughly balanced.
why_it_matters: That reading implies the Fed is still prioritizing inflation restraint over near-term labor-market support.

title: FedWatch - CME Group
evidence_text: CME FedWatch provides live market-implied probabilities for upcoming Fed rate outcomes based on Fed funds futures pricing.
why_it_matters: If futures and FedWatch probabilities are shifting toward smaller cut odds or hike odds, that signals the market expects a firmer Fed reaction to inflation or growth data.

title: 30 Day Federal Funds Futures Overview
evidence_text: CME lists 30-day federal funds futures as the underlying market used to infer expectations for the policy rate.
why_it_matters: A higher futures-implied path for the policy rate means markets are pricing fewer cuts or possible hikes, which tightens financial conditions.

title: Understanding the CME Group FedWatch Tool Methodology
evidence_text: CME explains that FedWatch converts 30-day Fed funds futures prices into implied probabilities for FOMC rate moves in 25-basis-point increments.
why_it_matters: This is the market-pricing mechanism behind cuts-priced-in versus hikes-priced-in framing, so it is the right tool for reading the Fed reaction-function signal.

title: CME FedWatch Tool User Guide
evidence_text: CME states that FedWatch analyzes the probability of FOMC rate moves for upcoming meetings.
why_it_matters: The tool directly maps futures pricing into expected policy outcomes, which is the core input for judging whether markets expect easing or tightening.

title: Understanding Fed Funds Futures: Trading, Settling, and Market Expectations
evidence_text: Fed funds futures prices reflect market expectations for future federal funds rate changes and can be translated into expected cuts or hikes.
why_it_matters: If those prices move higher, the implied policy path becomes more restrictive, which is consistent with fewer cuts or more hikes.

title: Treasury yields jump as traders reduce expectations for any 2026 Fed rate cuts
evidence_text: The piece says traders cut back expectations for 2026 Fed rate cuts and began pricing a possible rate increase in April plus a sequence of hikes by December.
why_it_matters: That kind of repricing suggests markets see a more hawkish Fed reaction-function path, with fewer cuts and potential tightening.

title: Federal Reserve: Extended pause guidance
evidence_text: The note says OIS swaps were pricing roughly a one-third probability of a 25 bp hike at the July 29 FOMC meeting.
why_it_matters: A priced-in hike probability implies markets were not fully positioned for near-term easing, which reduces the odds of a cut at the next meeting.
